title: Module review
subtitle: Everything from Reading the Label
objectives: Interpret European and New World systems

steps.prompt: In the EU, a stated vintage means at least what share of grapes from that year?
steps.explanation: 85% in the EU, and in many New World countries too.

steps.prompt: Match each term to its country.
steps.explanation: Every country has its own terms for protected places.

steps.prompt: A PGI wine has stricter rules than a PDO wine.
steps.explanation: Not true. PDO is stricter; PGI covers larger areas with looser rules.

steps.prompt: Order these sparkling wine terms from driest to sweetest.
steps.explanation: Extra Dry is sweeter than Brut, which surprises many people.

steps.prompt: Which of these are usually defined by law?
steps.explanation: Gran Reserva and Organic are regulated. Old Vines and US Reserve generally aren't.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels must show producer, origin, abv, volume and allergens
PDO is stricter than PGI; each country names them differently
New World GIs define area only
Ageing and sweetness terms are regulated; many others are marketing
